issues.legal_issue: Income from property acquired by a wife through an interconnected chain of transfers originating with her husband is income arising indirectly from assets transferred by the husband.
material_facts: A firm initially agreed to purchase a house, and the purchase was completed in the names of the husband’s wife, another partner’s wife, and a partner.

The women obtained funds through the firm that were recorded as gifts from close family members: in one instance, the husband’s son gave money to his mother, and in the other, the husband gave money to his daughter-in-law.
The gifts were of matching amounts and were made around the time of the purchase; the stated occasions for the gifts were not satisfactorily explained.
The women repaid the firm for their shares, including amounts their respective husbands had contributed toward the earnest money.
The Tribunal found that the women had acquired their shares from assets indirectly transferred by their husbands, and the property generated income assessed in the husbands’ hands.
issues.conclusion: The transfers were interconnected parts of a single circuitous transaction, so the women’s property income arose indirectly from assets transferred by their husbands and was includible in the husbands’ income.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 16(3)(a)(iii) of the Indian Income-tax Act, 1922, a wife’s income arising directly or indirectly from assets transferred to her by her husband, otherwise than for adequate consideration or in connection with an agreement to live apart, is included in the husband’s total income. The assets reaching the wife need not be the identical assets originally belonging to the husband. Interconnected transfers forming parts of one transaction and employing a circuitous device to avoid the provision fall within “indirectly”; technical consideration between the transfers is not required. No earlier cases are relied on in the judgment.

rule.if: spousal_income_tax_assessment and wife_acquired_income_producing_property and husband_assets_routed_through_relative and transfers_interconnected_as_circuitous_transaction

predicates.spousal_income_tax_assessment: A tax assessment concerns whether income from property held by a wife is to be treated as income of her husband.
predicates.wife_acquired_income_producing_property: A wife acquired an interest in property that produced income.
predicates.husband_assets_routed_through_relative: The husband’s assets were routed through a relative or other connected person before funds reached the wife for the acquisition.
predicates.transfers_interconnected_as_circuitous_t: The transfers were connected in timing, amount, or circumstances so that they formed a circuitous transaction rather than independent transfers.
predicates.wife_property_income_included_in_husband: The income from the wife’s property is included in the husband’s income.

issues.definition: When a wife acquires income-producing property using her husband’s assets routed through a connected person as part of an interconnected circuitous transaction in a spousal income-tax assessment, the property income is included in her husband’s income.
